paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The God who says "Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool" (Isaiah 66:1) doesn't need anything we build for Him. He says His own hand made all these things (Isaiah 66:2). So the one He esteems is "he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word" (Isaiah 66:2).

That's why the offerings in verse 3 got such a hard word. The people were bringing them, but the LORD says they "have chosen their own ways" (Isaiah 66:3). He also says He called and no one answered, and He spoke and no one listened (Isaiah 66:4). Church-looking stuff is not the same as listening, baker. The LORD wants a heart that hears Him, and I'd rather have a heart like that than the fanciest offering on the counter.

And look where the passage lands, because it lands SOFT. To those who tremble at His word, even when others exclude them over His name, He promises to finish what He started (Isaiah 66:5, 9). He will extend peace like a river, and "As a mother comforts her son, so will I comfort you" (Isaiah 66:12-13). His hand is revealed to His servants, and His wrath to His enemies (Isaiah 66:14), so listen to Him, friend, and let Him carry you.
